translations.literal: Wang Jin was at first also granted suicide; Liu Yan said to Li Han and the others: 「By precedent, heavy punishments require review and report; how much more for great ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin was at first also granted suicide; Liu Yan said to Li Han and the others: 「By precedent, heavy punishments require review and report to the throne; how much more for great ministers!

sentences.zh: 且法有首從，宜更稟進止。」

translations.literal: Moreover the law distinguishes principal and accessories; we ought to report again for instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the law distinguishes principal and accessories; we ought to report again for instructions.

sentences.zh: 涵等從之。

translations.literal: 」Han and the others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Han and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 上乃貶縉括州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon demoted Jin to Prefect of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon demoted Jin to Prefect of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 載妻王氏，忠嗣之女也，及子伯和、仲武、季能皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zai's wife Lady Wang was Zhongsi's daughter; together with sons Bohe, Zhongwu, and Jineng all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zai's wife Lady Wang was Zhongsi's daughter; together with sons Bohe, Zhongwu, and Jineng, all were executed.

sentences.zh: 有司籍載家財，胡椒至八百石，它物稱是。

translations.literal: The officials registered Zai's household property; pepper alone reached eight hundred piculs, and other goods were comparable.
translations.idiomatic: The officials registered Zai's household property; pepper alone reached eight hundred piculs, and other goods were comparable.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬午，以太常卿楊綰為中書侍郎，禮部侍郎常袞為門下侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renwu, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Guan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites Chang Fu was made Vice Director of the Chancellery; both were Co-Rank Directors.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day renwu, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yang Guan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Rites Chang Fu was made Vice Director of the Chancellery; both were Co-Rank Directors.

sentences.zh: 綰性清簡儉素，制下之日，朝野相賀。

translations.literal: Guan by nature was pure, simple, and frugal; on the day the appointment was issued, court and commoners alike congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was by nature pure, simple, and frugal; on the day the appointment was issued, court and commoners alike rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀方宴客，聞之，減坐中聲樂五分之四。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was just then feasting guests; hearing of it, he reduced the music at his table by four-fifths.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was just then feasting guests; hearing of it, he reduced the music at his table by four-fifths.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹黎幹，騶從甚盛，即日省之，止存十騎。

translations.literal: Li Gan, Prefect of Jingzhao, had a very grand mounted escort; that same day he reduced it, keeping only ten riders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, Prefect of Jingzhao, had a very grand mounted escort; that same day he reduced it, keeping only ten riders.

sentences.zh: 十丞崔寬，第捨宏侈，亟毀撤之。

translations.literal: Deputy Prefect Cui Kuan's residence was grand and extravagant; he quickly demolished and removed it.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Prefect Cui Kuan's residence was grand and extravagant; he quickly demolished it.

sentences.zh: 癸未，貶吏部侍郎楊炎、諫議大夫韓洄、包佶、起居舍人韓會等十餘人，皆載黨也。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Yan, Remonstrance Councilors Han Hui, Bao Ji, Diarist Han Hui, and more than ten others were demoted; all were Zai's faction.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei, Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Yan, Remonstrance Councilors Han Hui, Bao Ji, Diarist Han Hui, and more than ten others were demoted; all were members of Zai's faction.

sentences.zh: 炎，鳳翔人。

translations.literal: Yan was a man of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a native of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 載常引有文學才望者一人親厚之，異日欲以代己，故炎及於貶。

translations.literal: Zai often drew close one man of literary talent and reputation, treating him with special favor, intending someday to have him replace himself; therefore Yan came to demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Zai often drew close one man of literary talent and reputation, treating him with special favor and intending someday to have him replace himself; therefore Yan came to be demoted.

sentences.zh: 洄，滉之弟。

translations.literal: Hui was Huang's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was Huang's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 會，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Hui was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a native of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 上初欲盡誅炎等，吳湊諫救百端，始貶官。

translations.literal: The emperor at first wished to execute Yan and the others entirely; Wu Cou remonstrated in every way to save them, and only then were they demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first wished to execute Yan and the others entirely; Wu Cou remonstrated in every way to save them, and only then were they demoted.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，吐蕃寇黎、雅州；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Tibet raided Li and Ya prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Tibet raided Li and Ya prefectures;

sentences.zh: 西川節度使崔寧擊破之。

translations.literal: Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan Circuit, struck and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan Circuit, struck and routed them.

sentences.zh: 元載以仕進者多樂京師，惡其逼己，乃制俸祿，厚外官而薄京官，京官不能自給，常從外官乞貸。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai, because many seeking advancement delighted in the capital and he hated their pressing upon himself, then regulated salaries, making outer officials rich and capital officials poor; capital officials could not support themselves and often borrowed from outer officials.
translations.idiomatic: Because many seeking advancement preferred the capital, Yuan Zai, hating their pressure on himself, regulated salaries to favor outer officials and stint capital officials; capital officials could not support themselves and often had to borrow from outer officials.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞奏京官俸太薄；

translations.literal: Yang Guan and Chang Fu memorialized that capital officials' salaries were too thin;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan and Chang Fu memorialized that capital officials' salaries were too thin;

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔加京官俸，歲約十五萬六千餘緡。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, an edict increased capital officials' salaries, about one hundred fifty-six thousand-plus strings of cash per year in all.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiyou, an edict increased capital officials' salaries by about one hundred fifty-six thousand strings of cash per year in all.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛亥，詔自都團練使外，悉罷諸州團練守捉使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day xinhai, an edict ordered that apart from metropolitan training commissioners, all prefectural training and garrison commissioners be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day xinhai, an edict ordered that apart from metropolitan training commissioners, all prefectural training and garrison commissioners be abolished.

sentences.zh: 又令諸使非軍事要急，無得擅召刺史及停其職務，差人權攝。

translations.literal: It also ordered that circuit commissioners, unless military affairs were urgent, were not permitted on their own authority to summon prefects or suspend their duties and dispatch men to hold office in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered that circuit commissioners, unless military affairs were urgent, were not permitted on their own authority to summon prefects, suspend their duties, or dispatch men to hold office in their stead.

sentences.zh: 又定諸州兵，皆有常數，其召募給家糧、春冬衣者，謂之「官健」；

translations.literal: It also fixed the troops of all prefectures, each with a set quota; those recruited and given household grain rations and spring and winter clothing were called 「regular troops」;
translations.idiomatic: It also fixed troop quotas for all prefectures; those recruited and given household grain rations and spring and winter clothing were called 「regular troops」;

sentences.zh: 差點土人，春夏歸農、秋冬追集、給身糧醬菜者，謂之「團結」。

translations.literal: Local men drafted, who in spring and summer returned to farming and in autumn and winter were summoned and assembled and given personal grain rations and pickled vegetables, were called 「levied militia.」
translations.idiomatic: Local men drafted, who in spring and summer returned to farming and in autumn and winter were summoned and assembled and given personal grain rations and pickled vegetables, were called 「levied militia.」

sentences.zh: 自兵興以來，州縣官俸給不一，重以元載、王縉隨情徇私，刺史月給或至千緡、或數十緡，至是，始定節度使以下至主簿、尉俸祿，掊多益寡，上下有敘，法制粗立。

translations.literal: Since troops had risen, prefectural and county officials' salary allotments had not been uniform; compounded by Yuan Zai and Wang Jin indulging feelings and showing favoritism, prefects' monthly allotments might reach a thousand strings of cash or only several tens; now at last salaries were fixed from military governors down to recorders and assistant magistrates, taking from the many to supplement the few, with order above and below; the legal system was roughly established.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, prefectural and county officials' salary allotments had not been uniform; compounded by Yuan Zai and Wang Jin indulging favoritism, prefects' monthly allotments might reach a thousand strings of cash or only several tens; now at last salaries were fixed from military governors down to recorders and assistant magistrates, taking from the many to supplement the few, with order above and below, and the legal system was roughly established.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上遣中使發元載祖父墓，斫棺棄屍，毀其家廟，焚其木主。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the emperor dispatched palace envoys to open the graves of Zai's grandfather and father, chop open the coffins and discard the corpses, destroy the family temple, and burn the spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, the emperor dispatched palace envoys to open the graves of Zai's grandfather and father, chop open the coffins and discard the corpses, destroy the family temple, and burn the spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，卓英倩等皆杖死。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, Zhuo Yingqian and the others were all beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin, Zhuo Yingqian and the others were all beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 英倩之用事也，弟英璘橫於鄉里。

translations.literal: While Yingqian held power, his younger brother Yinglin was overbearing in the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: While Yingqian held power, his younger brother Yinglin was overbearing in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 及英倩下獄，英璘遂據險作亂；

translations.literal: When Yingqian was imprisoned, Yinglin thereupon seized defensible terrain and raised a disturbance;
translations.idiomatic: When Yingqian was imprisoned, Yinglin thereupon seized defensible terrain and raised a disturbance;

sentences.zh: 上發禁兵討之，乙巳，金州刺史孫道平擊擒之。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched palace troops to attack him; on the day yisi, Sun Daoping, prefect of Jin Prefecture, struck and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched palace troops to attack him; on the day yisi, Sun Daoping, prefect of Jin Prefecture, struck and captured him.

sentences.zh: 上方倚楊綰，使釐革弊政，會綰有疾，秋，七月，己巳，薨。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then relying on Yang Guan to reform corrupt government; it happened that Guan fell ill; in autumn, the seventh month, on the day jisi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just then relying on Yang Guan to reform corrupt government when Guan fell ill; in autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jisi, he died.

sentences.zh: 上痛悼之甚，謂群臣曰：「天不欲朕致太平，何奪朕楊綰之速！」

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply and said to the assembled ministers: 「Heaven does not wish me to attain peace—why take Yang Guan from me so soon!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and said to the assembled ministers: 「Heaven does not wish me to attain peace—why take Yang Guan from me so soon!"

sentences.zh: 八月，癸未，賜東川節度使鮮于叔明姓李氏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day guiwei, the surname Li was granted to Xianyu Shuming, military governor of Dongchuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day guiwei, the surname Li was granted to Xianyu Shuming, military governor of Dongchuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元載、王縉之為相也，上日賜以內廚御饌，可食十人，遂為故事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai and Wang Jin served as chancellors, the emperor daily granted them imperial kitchen fare from the inner kitchen, enough to feed ten men; this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai and Wang Jin served as chancellors, the emperor daily granted them imperial kitchen fare from the inner kitchen, enough to feed ten men; this became precedent.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，常袞與朱泚上言：「餐錢已多，乞停賜饌。」

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Chang Fu and Zhu Ci submitted a memorial: 「Meal allowances are already ample; we beg to stop the grant of imperial fare.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Chang Fu and Zhu Ci submitted a memorial: 「Meal allowances are already ample; we beg to stop the grant of imperial fare.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: 」It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: 」The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 袞又欲辭堂封，同列不可而止。

translations.literal: Fu again wished to decline the chancellors' supplemental salary; his colleagues would not permit it, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fu again wished to decline the chancellors' supplemental salary; his colleagues would not permit it, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 時人諷袞，以為「朝廷厚祿，所以養賢，不能，當辭位，不當辭祿。」

translations.literal: People of the time satirized Fu, saying 「The court's generous salary is meant to support the worthy; if one is not capable, one ought to resign office, not decline salary."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time satirized Fu, saying 「The court's generous salary is meant to support the worthy; if one is not capable, one ought to resign office, not decline salary."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「君子恥食浮於人；

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: 「A gentleman is ashamed to eat more lavishly than others;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang says: 「A gentleman is ashamed to eat more lavishly than others;

sentences.zh: 袞之辭祿，廉恥存焉，與夫固位貪祿者，不猶愈乎！

translations.literal: Fu's declining salary still preserves integrity and shame—compared with those who cling to office and greedily hold salary, is it not still better!
translations.idiomatic: Fu's declining salary still preserves integrity and shame—compared with those who cling to office and greedily hold salary, is it not still better!

sentences.zh: 詩云：『彼君子兮，不素餐兮！』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 『That gentleman there—he does not eat idle meals!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 『That gentleman there—he does not eat idle meals!

sentences.zh: 如袞者，亦未可以深譏也。

translations.literal: 』One like Fu likewise cannot be deeply ridiculed.
translations.idiomatic: 』One like Fu likewise cannot be deeply ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 楊綰、常袞薦湖州刺史顏真卿，上即日召還；

translations.literal: Yang Guan and Chang Fu recommended Yan Zhenqing, Prefect of Huzhou; the emperor that same day summoned him back;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan and Chang Fu recommended Yan Zhenqing, Prefect of Huzhou; the emperor that same day summoned him back;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, he was made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 綰、袞又薦淮南判官汲人關播，擢為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Guan and Fu again recommended Guan Bo of Ji, adjutant of Huainan; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Office for Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Fu again recommended Guan Bo of Ji, adjutant of Huainan; he was promoted to Vice Director of the Office for Punishments.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，以四鎮、北庭行營兼涇原、鄭穎節度副使段秀實為節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day xinyou, Duan Xiushi, deputy military governor of the Four Garrisons and Beiting Field Army and concurrently of Jingyuan and Zheng-Ying circuits, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day xinyou, Duan Xiushi, deputy military governor of the Four Garrisons and Beiting Field Army and concurrently of Jingyuan and Zheng-Ying circuits, was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 秀實軍令簡約，有威惠，奉身清儉，室無姬妾，非公會，未嘗飲酒聽樂。

translations.literal: Xiushi's military orders were simple and concise; he had authority and kindness; he conducted himself purely and frugally; his household had no concubines; except at official gatherings he never drank wine or listened to music.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushi's military orders were simple and concise; he had both authority and kindness; he conducted himself purely and frugally; his household had no concubines; except at official gatherings he never drank wine or listened to music.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃八萬眾軍於原州北長澤監，己巳，破方渠，入拔谷；

translations.literal: Eighty thousand Tibetans encamped at Changze Post north of Yuan Prefecture; on the day jisi they broke Fangqu and entered Bagu;
translations.idiomatic: Eighty thousand Tibetans encamped at Changze Post north of Yuan Prefecture; on the day jisi they broke through Fangqu and entered Bagu;

sentences.zh: 郭子儀使裨將李懷光救之，吐蕃退。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi sent Lieutenant General Li Huaiguang to rescue them; Tibet withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent Lieutenant General Li Huaiguang to rescue them; the Tibetans withdrew.

sentences.zh: 庚午，吐蕃寇坊州。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Tibet raided Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu, Tibet raided Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，西川節度使崔寧奏大破吐蕃於望漢城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day yiyou, Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan Circuit, memorialized a great rout of Tibet at Wanghancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the day yiyou, Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan Circuit, memorialized a great rout of the Tibetans at Wanghancheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，秋霖，河中府池鹽多敗。

translations.literal: Earlier, autumn rains had caused much of the pond salt of Hezhong Prefecture to spoil.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, autumn rains had caused much of the pond salt of Hezhong Prefecture to spoil.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎判度支韓滉恐鹽戶減稅，丁亥，奏雨雖多，不害鹽，仍有瑞鹽生。

translations.literal: Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Department of Public Works, feared salt households would reduce taxes; on the day dinghai he memorialized that though rain was heavy, it did not harm the salt, and auspicious salt still formed.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Department of Public Works, feared salt households would reduce taxes; on the day dinghai he memorialized that though rain was heavy, it did not harm the salt, and auspicious salt still formed.

sentences.zh: 上疑其不然，遣諫議大夫義興蔣鎮往視之。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted this was so and dispatched Remonstrance Councilor Jiang Zhen of Yixing to go inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted this was so and dispatched Remonstrance Councilor Jiang Zhen of Yixing to go inspect it.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇鹽、夏州，又寇長武；

translations.literal: Tibet raided Yan and Xia prefectures and again raided Changwu;
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans raided Yan and Xia prefectures and again raided Changwu;

sentences.zh: 郭子儀遣將拒卻之。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi dispatched generals to repel and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi dispatched generals to repel and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 以永平軍押牙匡城劉洽為宋州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Qia of Kuangcheng, adjutant of Yongping Army, was made Prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia of Kuangcheng, adjutant of Yongping Army, was appointed Prefect of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仍以宋、泗二州隸永平軍。

translations.literal: Song and Si prefectures were still placed under Yongping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Si prefectures were still placed under Yongping Army.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹黎幹奏秋霖損稼，韓滉奏幹不實；

translations.literal: Li Gan, Prefect of Jingzhao, memorialized that autumn rains had damaged the crops; Han Huang memorialized that Gan's report was untrue;
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, Prefect of Jingzhao, memorialized that autumn rains had damaged the crops; Han Huang memorialized that Gan's report was untrue;

sentences.zh: 上命御史按視，丁未，還奏，「所損凡三萬餘頃。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered censors to inspect on site; on the day dingwei they returned and memorialized, "The damage in all exceeds thirty thousand qing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered censors to inspect on site; on the day dingwei they returned and reported, "The total damage exceeds thirty thousand qing."

sentences.zh: 渭南令劉澡阿附度支，稱縣境苗獨不損；

translations.literal: Weinan Magistrate Liu Zao curried favor with the Treasury Commission and declared that crops within the county alone were undamaged;
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Weinan, Liu Zao, curried favor with the Treasury Commission and claimed that crops in his county alone had suffered no damage;

sentences.zh: 御史趙計奏與澡同。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Ji memorialized the same as Zao.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Ji submitted a memorial agreeing with Zao.

sentences.zh: 上曰「霖雨溥溥，豈得渭南獨無！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The autumn rains were widespread—how could Weinan alone have none!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The autumn rains fell far and wide—how could Weinan alone have escaped them!"

sentences.zh: 更命御史朱敖視之，損三千餘頃。

translations.literal: He ordered Censor Zhu Ao to inspect again; the damage exceeded three thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Censor Zhu Ao to inspect again and found damage exceeding three thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 上歎息久之，曰：「縣令，字人之官，不損猶應言損，乃不仁如是乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed long and said, "The magistrate is an office of caring for the people—even if there were no damage he ought still to speak of damage; could unkindness go so far as this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed for a long while and said, "A magistrate is an officer charged with nurturing the people—even when there is no damage he should still report damage; could anyone be so devoid of compassion!"

sentences.zh: 貶澡南浦尉，計澧州司戶，而不問滉。

translations.literal: Zao was demoted to Wei of Nanpu; Ji was made Records Officer of Lizhou—but Huang was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was demoted to captain of Nanpu; Ji was made records officer of Lizhou—but Han Huang was not questioned.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，山南西道節度使張獻恭奏破吐蕃萬餘眾於岷州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renzi, Shannan West Circuit military governor Zhang Xiangong memorialized that he had defeated more than ten thousand Tibetans at Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day renzi, Shannan West Circuit military governor Zhang Xiangong reported defeating more than ten thousand Tibetans at Min Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 內辰，蔣鎮還，奏「瑞鹽實如韓滉所言」，仍上表賀，請宣付史臣，並置神祠，錫以嘉名。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Jiang Zhen returned and memorialized, "The auspicious salt is indeed as Han Huang said," and moreover submitted a congratulatory memorial, requesting that it be proclaimed to the historiographers, that a spirit shrine be established, and that an honorable name be bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Jiang Zhen returned and reported, "The auspicious salt is exactly as Han Huang described," and submitted a congratulatory memorial asking that the matter be proclaimed to the historiographers, that a spirit shrine be established, and that an honorable name be granted.

sentences.zh: 上從之，賜號寶應靈慶池。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and bestowed the name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and bestowed the name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pool.

sentences.zh: 時人醜之。

translations.literal: People of the time found it shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded the affair with disgust.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙戌，朱泚自涇州還京師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day bingxu, Zhu Ci returned to the capital from Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day bingxu, Zhu Ci returned to the capital from Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，崔寧奏破吐蕃十餘萬眾，斬首八千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Cui Ning memorialized that he had defeated more than one hundred thousand Tibetans and taken more than eight thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Cui Ning reported defeating more than one hundred thousand Tibetans and taking over eight thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以朱泚兼隴右節度使，知河西、澤潞行營。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Zhu Ci was made concurrent military governor of Longyou and placed in command of the He-Xi and Ze-Lu field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, Zhu Ci was appointed concurrent military governor of Longyou and given command of the He-Xi and Ze-Lu field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使李正己先有淄、青、齊、海、登、萊、沂、密、德、棣十州之地，及李靈曜之亂，諸道合兵攻之，所得之地，各為己有，正己又得曹、濮、徐、兗、鄆五州，因自青州徙治鄆州，使其子前淄州刺史納守青州。

translations.literal: Pinglu military governor Li Zhengyi had earlier held the ten prefectures of Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di; when Li Lingyao rebelled, the various circuits joined forces to attack him, and each kept for himself the territory gained—Zhengyi moreover gained the five prefectures of Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun; he therefore moved his seat from Qing Prefecture to Yun Prefecture and had his son Na, former prefect of Zi, hold Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu military governor Li Zhengyi already held ten prefectures—Zi, Qing, Qi, Hai, Deng, Lai, Yi, Mi, De, and Di. During Li Lingyao's rebellion the various circuits joined in attacking him, and each kept whatever territory it seized; Zhengyi also gained Cao, Pu, Xu, Yan, and Yun. He therefore moved his headquarters from Qing Prefecture to Yun Prefecture and left his son Na, the former prefect of Zi, to hold Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以納為青州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Na was made prefect of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guimao, Na was appointed prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 正己用刑嚴峻，所在不敢偶語；

translations.literal: Zhengyi applied punishments with severity; wherever he ruled no one dared speak even in pairs;
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyi enforced the law with brutal severity; throughout his domain no one dared whisper in pairs;

sentences.zh: 然法令齊一，賦均而輕，擁兵十萬，雄據東方，鄰籓皆畏之。

translations.literal: yet his laws and orders were uniform, taxes even and light; he held a hundred thousand troops, dominated the east in power, and neighboring circuits all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: yet his laws were uniform, his taxes fair and light, his army numbered one hundred thousand, he held the east in lordly power, and neighboring circuits all feared him.

sentences.zh: 是時田承嗣據魏、博、相、衛、洺、貝、澶七州，李寶臣據恆、易、趙、定、深、冀、滄七州，各擁眾五萬；

translations.literal: At this time Tian Chengsi held the seven prefectures of Weizhou, Bo, Xiang, Wei, Ming, Bei, and Chan; Li Baochen held the seven prefectures of Heng, Yi, Zhao, Ding, Shen, Ji, and Cang—each with fifty thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: At this time Tian Chengsi held Weizhou, Bo, Xiang, Wei Prefecture, Ming, Bei, and Chan—seven prefectures—and Li Baochen held Heng, Yi, Zhao, Ding, Shen, Ji, and Cang—seven prefectures; each commanded fifty thousand men;

sentences.zh: 梁崇義據襄、鄧、均、房、復、郢六州，有眾二萬；

translations.literal: Liang Chongyi held the six prefectures of Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Fu, and Ying, with twenty thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chongyi held Xiang, Deng, Jun, Fang, Fu, and Ying—six prefectures—with twenty thousand men;

sentences.zh: 相與根據蟠結，雖奉事朝廷而不用其法令，官爵、甲兵、租賦、刑殺皆自專之，上寬仁，一聽其所為。

translations.literal: They mutually rooted themselves and intertwined; though they served the court they did not use its laws and orders—office, rank, armor, troops, taxes, and punishments they all monopolized for themselves; the emperor was lenient and benevolent and let them do as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They entrenched themselves and bound one another together; though they nominally served the court they ignored its laws, reserving to themselves appointments, arms, taxes, and punishments. The emperor was lenient and indulgent and let them have their way.

sentences.zh: 朝廷或完一城，增一兵，輒有怨言，以為猜貳，常為之罷役；

translations.literal: If the court repaired a city or added a soldier, they at once voiced complaints, taking it as suspicion and disloyalty, and the court often stopped such work for their sake;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court repaired a city or added a single soldier, they complained at once, calling it a sign of distrust, and the court often abandoned such projects to appease them;

sentences.zh: 而自於境內築壘、繕兵無虛日。

translations.literal: yet within their own borders they built fortifications and readied troops without a single idle day.
translations.idiomatic: yet within their own territories they built fortifications and drilled troops without a day's rest.

sentences.zh: 以是雖在中國名蕃臣，而實如蠻貊異域焉。

translations.literal: Thus though within China they were called frontier vassals, in reality they were like barbarian lands beyond the pale.
translations.idiomatic: Thus, though within the empire they were styled frontier vassals, in truth they were as foreign as the lands of the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝中之下大曆十三年（

translations.literal: Mid-to-Lower of Emperor Daizong the Sage Filial Martial, Thirteenth Year of Dali (
translations.idiomatic: Mid-to-Lower of Emperor Daizong the Sage Filial Martial, Thirteenth Year of Dali (

sentences.zh: 戊午，公元七七八年）

translations.literal: wuwu, 778 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuwu, 778 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，敕毀白渠支流碾磑以溉田。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinyou, an edict ordered the destruction of watermills on the branch channels of the White Canal so that fields might be irrigated.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day xinyou, an edict ordered the destruction of watermills on the White Canal's branch channels to free water for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 昇平公主有二磑，入見於上，請存之。

translations.literal: Princess Shengping had two watermills; she entered audience with the emperor and requested that they be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shengping owned two watermills; she came before the emperor and asked that they be spared.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾欲以利蒼主，汝識吾意，當為眾先。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I wish to benefit the common people; you understand my intent—take the lead among all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I mean this for the good of the people; you understand my intent—set the example for everyone."

sentences.zh: 公主即日毀之。

translations.literal: That same day the princess destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the princess had them destroyed.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，回紇寇太原，河東押牙泗水李自良曰：「回紇精銳遠來求鬥，難與爭鋒；

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the Uyghurs raided Taiyuan; Hedong adjutant Li Ziliang of Sishui said, "The Uyghurs are elite troops who have come from afar seeking battle—it is hard to contend with them at the spearpoint;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen, the Uyghurs raided Taiyuan. Hedong adjutant Li Ziliang of Sishui said, "The Uyghurs are crack troops who have marched far to fight; it is unwise to meet them head-on;

sentences.zh: 不如築二壘於歸路，以兵戍之。

translations.literal: it would be better to build two forts on their line of retreat and garrison them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Better to build two forts on their line of retreat and garrison them with troops.

sentences.zh: 虜至，堅壁勿與戰，彼師老自歸，乃出軍乘之。

translations.literal: When the barbarians arrive, hold the walls and do not give battle; when their army grows weary and withdraws of itself, then send troops out to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrives, hold the walls and refuse battle; once their army grows weary and turns homeward, then sally out and strike them.

sentences.zh: 二壘抗其前，大軍蹙其後，無不捷矣。」

translations.literal: The two forts will block them in front and the main army will press them from behind—there will be no battle that is not victorious."
translations.idiomatic: With the two forts blocking them in front and the main army pressing from behind, victory is assured."

sentences.zh: 留後鮑防不從，遣大將焦伯瑜等逆戰；

translations.literal: Acting military governor Bao Fang did not follow this; he dispatched great generals Jiao Boyu and others to give battle;
translations.idiomatic: Acting military governor Bao Fang refused; he sent his chief generals Jiao Boyu and others to meet the enemy in battle;

sentences.zh: 癸酉，遇虜於陽曲，大敗而還，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: on the day guiyou they met the barbarians at Yangqu, were utterly defeated and returned, and more than ten thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: on the day guiyou they met the enemy at Yangqu, suffered a crushing defeat, and lost more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 回紇縱兵大掠。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs let their troops plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs unleashed their troops to plunder at will.

sentences.zh: 二月，代州都督張光晟擊破之於羊武谷，乃引去。

translations.literal: In the second month, Daizhou area commander Zhang Guangcheng defeated them at Yangwu Valley, and they thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Daizhou area commander Zhang Guangcheng routed them at Yangwu Valley, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上引去。

translations.literal: The emperor let them withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let them withdraw without further pursuit.

sentences.zh: 上亦不問回紇入寇之故，待之如初。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not inquire into the reason for the Uyghur raid and treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor likewise made no inquiry into why the Uyghurs had raided and treated them exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 己亥，吐蕃遣其將馬重英帥眾四萬寇靈州，塞填漢、御史、尚書三渠水口以弊屯田。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Tibet sent its general Ma Chongying to lead forty thousand men to raid Ling Prefecture, blocking and filling the mouths of the Han, Yushi, and Shangshu canals to cripple the garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, Tibet sent General Ma Chongying at the head of forty thousand men to raid Ling Prefecture, damming the Han, Yushi, and Shangshu canal outlets to ruin the frontier farms.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，回紇使還，過河中，朔方軍士掠其輜重，因大掠坊市。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiaxu, Uyghur envoys returned; passing through Hezhong, Shuofang soldiers plundered their baggage train and thereupon looted the markets on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jiaxu, Uyghur envoys were returning home; passing through Hezhong, Shuofang soldiers plundered their baggage train and then looted the city markets.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲辰，吐蕃寇靈州，朔方留後常謙光擊破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiachen, Tibet raided Ling Prefecture; Shuofang acting military governor Chang Qianguang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day jiachen, Tibet raided Ling Prefecture; Shuofang acting military governor Chang Qianguang routed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊戌，隴右節度使朱泚獻貓鼠同乳不相害者以為瑞；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day wuxu, Longyou military governor Zhu Ci presented a cat and a rat nursing from the same mother without harming each other as an auspicious sign;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day wuxu, Longyou military governor Zhu Ci presented as an omen a cat and a rat nursing from the same mother without harming each other;

sentences.zh: 常袞帥百官稱賀。

translations.literal: Chang Fu led the hundred officials in offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Fu led the hundred officials in offering congratulations.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人崔祐甫獨不賀，曰：「物反常為妖，貓捕鼠，乃其職也，今同乳，妖也。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat drafter Cui Youfu alone did not congratulate them and said, "When things depart from the norm they become portents; cats catch rats—that is their office—yet now they nurse together: this is a portent.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat drafter Cui Youfu alone refused to join the congratulations and said, "When things violate the natural order they become omens. Cats hunt rats—that is their nature—yet now they nurse together; this is an omen.

sentences.zh: 何乃賀為！

translations.literal: Why offer congratulations for it!
translations.idiomatic: Why should we congratulate it!

sentences.zh: 宜戒法吏之不察奸、邊吏之不禦寇者，以承天意。」

translations.literal: One ought rather to warn law officers who fail to detect treachery and frontier officers who fail to repel raiders, so as to accord with Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: We ought instead to warn law officers who fail to detect treachery and frontier officers who fail to repel invaders, so as to heed Heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 祐甫，沔之子也。

translations.literal: Youfu was the son of Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu was the son of Cui Mian.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬子，以祐甫知吏部選事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renzi, Youfu was put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day renzi, Youfu was placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection of officials.

sentences.zh: 祐甫數以公事與常袞爭，由是惡之。

translations.literal: Youfu repeatedly disputed official business with Chang Fu; for this reason Fu hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu repeatedly clashed with Chang Fu over official business, and for that reason Fu came to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 戊午，郭子儀奏以回紇猶在塞上，邊人恐懼，請遣邠州刺史渾瑊將兵鎮振武軍，從之。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Guo Ziyi memorialized that because the Uyghurs were still on the frontier the border people were afraid, and requested that Bin Prefecture prefect Hun Jian lead troops to garrison Zhenwu Army; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu, Guo Ziyi memorialized that with the Uyghurs still on the frontier the border people lived in fear, and asked that Bin Prefecture prefect Hun Jian be sent with troops to garrison Zhenwu Army; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 回紇始去。

translations.literal: Only then did the Uyghurs depart.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Uyghurs withdraw.

sentences.zh: 辛未，吐蕃將馬重英二萬眾寇鹽、慶二州，郭子儀遣河東朔方都虞候李懷光擊卻之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Tibetan general Ma Chongying with twenty thousand men raided Yan and Qing Prefectures; Guo Ziyi dispatched Hedong-Shuofang chief adjutant Li Huaiguang, who drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei, Tibetan general Ma Chongying led twenty thousand men against Yan and Qing Prefectures; Guo Ziyi sent Hedong-Shuofang chief adjutant Li Huaiguang, who repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙亥，成德節度使李寶臣請複姓張，許之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day yihai, Chengde military governor Li Baochen requested restoration of the surname Zhang; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day yihai, Chengde military governor Li Baochen asked to resume the surname Zhang; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃二萬眾寇銀、麟州、略党項雜畜，郭子儀遣李懷光等擊破之。

translations.literal: Twenty thousand Tibetans raided Yin and Lin Prefectures and carried off mixed livestock of the Tangut tribes; Guo Ziyi dispatched Li Huaiguang and others, who defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand Tibetans raided Yin and Lin Prefectures and drove off Tangut livestock; Guo Ziyi sent Li Huaiguang and others, who routed them.

sentences.zh: 上悼念貞懿皇后不已，殯於內殿，累年不忍葬；

translations.literal: The emperor mourned Empress Zhenyi without cease; her coffin lay in the inner hall and for years he could not bear to bury her;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not cease mourning Empress Zhenyi; her coffin remained in the inner hall, and for years he could not bring himself to bury her;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，始葬於莊陵。

translations.literal: on the day dingyou she was at last buried at Zhuang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: on the day dingyou she was at last interred at Zhuang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午，吐蕃萬騎下青石嶺，逼涇州；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day gengwu, ten thousand Tibetan horsemen descended Qingshi Ridge and pressed Jing Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day gengwu, ten thousand Tibetan horsemen came down Qingshi Ridge and threatened Jing Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 詔郭子儀、朱泚與段秀實共卻之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered Guo Ziyi, Zhu Ci, and Duan Xiushi jointly to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: an edict ordered Guo Ziyi, Zhu Ci, and Duan Xiushi to join in repulsing them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，丙戌，以吏部尚書、轉運、鹽鐵等使劉晏為左僕射，知三銓及使職如故。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day bingxu, Minister of Personnel and transport, salt, and iron commissioner Liu Yan was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State and continued in charge of the three selection boards and his commission duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day bingxu, Minister of Personnel and commissioner of transport, salt, and iron Liu Yan was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State, retaining charge of the three selection boards and his commission duties as before.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀入朝，命判官京兆杜黃裳主留務。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi came to court; he ordered his aide Du Huangshang of Jingzhao to take charge of affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi came to court and appointed his aide Du Huangshang of Jingzhao to manage affairs in his absence.

sentences.zh: 李懷光陰謀代子儀，矯為詔書，欲誅大將溫儒雅等。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang secretly plotted to replace Ziyi; he forged an imperial edict wishing to execute great generals Wen Ruya and others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiguang secretly plotted to supplant Guo Ziyi; he forged an imperial edict intending to execute the senior generals Wen Ruya and others.

sentences.zh: 黃裳察其詐，以詰懷光；

translations.literal: Huangshang detected the fraud and questioned Huaiguang;
translations.idiomatic: Huangshang detected the forgery and confronted Huaiguang;

sentences.zh: 懷光流汗伏罪。

translations.literal: Huaiguang sweated and submitted to guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiguang broke into a sweat and confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 於是諸將之難制者，黃裳矯子儀之命，皆出之於外，軍府乃安。

translations.literal: Thereupon, for the generals who were hard to control, Huangshang forged orders in Ziyi's name and sent them all outside; the army headquarters was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Huangshang, forging orders in Guo Ziyi's name, posted all the unruly generals outside the headquarters, and the army command was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 以給事中杜亞為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Palace provisioner Du Ya was made Jiangxi observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Palace provisioner Du Ya was appointed Jiangxi observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上召江西判官李泌入見，語以元載事，曰：「與卿別八年，乃能除此賊。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Jiangxi aide Li Bi for audience and spoke to him of Yuan Zai's affair, saying, "It has been eight years since I parted from you, and only now have you been able to remove this villain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Jiangxi aide Li Bi for an audience and spoke of Yuan Zai's case, saying, "Eight years have passed since we parted, and only now has this villain been removed.

sentences.zh: 賴太子發其陰謀，不然，幾不見卿。」

translations.literal: We relied on the crown prince to expose his secret plot—otherwise I would almost never have seen you again."
translations.idiomatic: We owe it to the crown prince for exposing his secret plot; otherwise I might never have seen you again."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣昔日固嘗言之。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your subject spoke of this in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Your subject warned of this long ago.

sentences.zh: 陛下知群臣有不善，則去之；

translations.literal: When Your Majesty knew that ministers and officials were unworthy, you removed them;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty knew that a minister was corrupt, you removed him;

sentences.zh: 含容太過，故至於此。」

translations.literal: but your forbearance went too far, and so matters came to this."
translations.idiomatic: but Your Majesty's forbearance went too far, and matters came to this pass."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「事亦應十全，不可輕發。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Matters ought also to be fully assured; one must not act lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Such matters must be fully assured; one must not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 上因言：「朕面屬卿於路嗣恭，而嗣恭取載意，奏卿為虔州別駕。

translations.literal: The emperor then said, "I personally charged you to Lu Sigong face to face, yet Sigong took Zai's side and memorialized to make you assistant prefect of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went on, "I personally entrusted you to Lu Sigong, yet Sigong followed Zai's wishes and had you posted as assistant prefect of Qian.

sentences.zh: 嗣恭初平嶺南，獻琉璃盤，逕九寸，朕以為至寶。

translations.literal: When Sigong first pacified Lingnan he presented a glass dish nine inches across; I took it for a supreme treasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Sigong first pacified Lingnan he presented a glass dish nine inches across, which I took to be a supreme treasure.

sentences.zh: 及破載家，得嗣恭所遺載琉璃盤，逕尺。

translations.literal: When Zai's household was searched, a glass dish Sigong had sent to Zai was found, a foot across.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai's household was searched, a glass dish Sigong had sent him was found—a full foot across.

sentences.zh: 俟其至，當與卿議之。」

translations.literal: When he arrives I shall discuss it with you."
translations.idiomatic: When he arrives I shall discuss the matter with you."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「嗣恭為人，小心，善事人，畏權勢，精勤吏事而不知大體。

translations.literal: Bi said, "Sigong as a man is cautious, good at serving others, fearful of power, diligent and exact in clerical affairs yet ignorant of larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Sigong is cautious by nature, skilled at pleasing others, fearful of power, meticulous in administrative detail yet blind to larger principles.

sentences.zh: 昔為縣令，有能名。

translations.literal: Formerly as a county magistrate he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: As a county magistrate he once enjoyed a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 陛下未暇知之，而為載所用，故為之盡力。

translations.literal: Your Majesty had not yet had leisure to know him, and Zai employed him, so he exerted himself fully for Zai.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had not yet had occasion to know him, and Zai made use of him, so he served Zai with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠知而用之，彼亦為陛下盡力矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly knows him and employs him, he too will exert himself fully for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly knows him and employs him, he will serve Your Majesty with equal devotion.

sentences.zh: 虔州別駕，臣自欲之，非其罪也。

translations.literal: The assistant prefectship of Qian—I myself desired it; it was not his fault.
translations.idiomatic: The post of assistant prefect of Qian—I asked for it myself; it was not his fault.

sentences.zh: 且嗣恭新立大功，陛下豈得以一琉璃盤罪之邪！」

translations.literal: Moreover Sigong has just achieved a great merit—how could Your Majesty punish him over a single glass dish!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Sigong has just won a great victory—surely Your Majesty would not punish him over a single glass dish!"

sentences.zh: 上意乃解，以嗣恭為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was then eased, and Sigong was made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger subsided, and Sigong was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以朔方節度副使張曇性剛率，謂其以武人輕己，銜之；

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, because Shuofang military governor deputy Zhang Tan was by nature blunt and forthright and he thought that as a military man Tan looked down on him, harbored resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi resented Zhang Tan, deputy military governor of Shuofang, because Tan was blunt and forthright by nature and Guo Ziyi believed that as a military man Tan looked down on him;

sentences.zh: 孔目官吳曜為子儀所任，因而構之。

translations.literal: clerk Wu Yao, whom Ziyi trusted, thereupon framed Tan.
translations.idiomatic: clerk Wu Yao, whom Guo Ziyi trusted, thereupon framed Tan.

sentences.zh: 子儀怒，誣奏曇扇動軍眾，誅之。

translations.literal: Ziyi grew angry, falsely memorialized that Tan had incited the army, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi flew into a rage, falsely accused Tan of inciting the troops, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 掌書記高郢力爭之，子儀不聽，奏貶郢猗氏丞。

translations.literal: chief secretary Gao Ying argued against this with all his strength; Ziyi would not listen and memorialized to demote Ying to assistant magistrate of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Gao Ying argued strenuously against it; Guo Ziyi would not listen and had Ying demoted to assistant magistrate of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 既而僚佐多以病求去，子儀悔之，悉薦之於朝，曰：「吳曜誤我。」

translations.literal: Before long many staff members requested leave on grounds of illness; Ziyi regretted it, recommended them all to the court, and said, "Wu Yao misled me."
translations.idiomatic: Before long many of his staff requested leave on grounds of illness; Guo Ziyi repented, recommended them all to the court, and said, "Wu Yao misled me."

sentences.zh: 遂逐之。

translations.literal: He thereupon drove Yao away.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove Wu Yao away.

sentences.zh: 常袞言於上曰：「陛下久欲用李泌，昔漢宣帝欲用人為公卿，必先試理人，請且以為刺史，使周知人間利病，俟報政而用之。」

translations.literal: Chang Fu spoke to the emperor, saying, "Your Majesty has long wished to employ Li Bi; in former times when Emperor Xuan of Han wished to use a man as minister or high official, he first tested him in governing people—I ask that for the time being he be made a prefect, so that he may thoroughly know the benefits and ills among the people, and when his term report comes in he may be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Chang Fu said to the emperor, "Your Majesty has long wished to employ Li Bi. When Emperor Xuan of Han wished to appoint a man to high office, he first tested him in governing the people. I ask that Li Bi be made a prefect for the time being, so that he may learn the people's hardships and blessings firsthand, and be appointed to higher office once his term report is in."

sentences.zh: 代宗睿文孝武皇帝中之下大曆十四年（

translations.literal: Mid-to-Lower of Emperor Daizong the Sage Filial Martial, Fourteenth Year of Dali (
translations.idiomatic: Mid-to-Lower of Emperor Daizong the Sage Filial Martial, Fourteenth Year of Dali (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元七七九年）

translations.literal: jiwei, 779 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiwei, 779 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，以李泌為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day renxu, Li Bi was made prefect of Li.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the day renxu, Li Bi was appointed prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸未，魏博節度使田承嗣薨。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day guimao, Weibo military governor Tian Chengsi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day guimao, Weibo military governor Tian Chengsi died.

sentences.zh: 有子十一人，以其侄中軍兵馬使悅為才，使知軍事，而諸子佐之。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; judging his nephew, Central Army horse-and-troop commander Yue, to be talented, he had him manage military affairs while the sons assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons; judging his nephew Yue, commander of the central army's horse and troop division, to be the ablest, he put him in charge of military affairs with his sons to assist.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以悅為魏博留後。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Yue was made acting military governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen, Yue was appointed acting military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 淮西節度使李忠臣，貪殘好色，將吏妻女美者，多逼淫之，悉以軍政委妹婿節度副使張惠光。

translations.literal: Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was greedy, cruel, and fond of women; when officers' and officials' wives and daughters were beautiful he often forced them to his bed, and he entrusted all military and administrative affairs to his sister's son-in-law, deputy military governor Zhang Huiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-Xi military governor Li Zhongchen was greedy, cruel, and licentious; whenever an officer's or official's wife or daughter was beautiful he often forced her into his bed, and he entrusted all military and civil affairs to his sister's son-in-law, deputy military governor Zhang Huiguang.

sentences.zh: 惠光挾勢暴橫，軍州苦之。

translations.literal: Huiguang relied on his power and was violent and overbearing; the armies and prefectures suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Huiguang abused his authority and ruled with violence; the garrison and prefectures groaned under him.

sentences.zh: 忠臣復以惠光子為牙將，暴橫甚於其父。

translations.literal: Zhongchen further appointed Huiguang's son as a ya-jiang; he was even more violent and overbearing than his father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen further appointed Huiguang's son as an assistant general, and the son was even more brutal and overbearing than his father.

sentences.zh: 左廂都虞候李希烈，忠臣之族子也，為眾所服。

translations.literal: Li Xilie, Left Wing Chief Commandant, was Zhongchen's clansman and was respected by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie, chief commandant of the left wing, was Zhongchen's clansman and enjoyed the troops' respect.

sentences.zh: 希烈因眾心怨怒，三月，丁未，與大將丁暠等殺惠光父子而逐忠臣。

translations.literal: Xilie, taking advantage of the troops' resentment and anger, in the third month on the day dingwei, together with the great general Ding Hao and others killed Huiguang and his son and drove out Zhongchen.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the troops' anger, Xilie joined the great general Ding Hao and others on the day dingwei in the third month to kill Huiguang and his son and drive Zhongchen out.

sentences.zh: 忠臣單騎奔京師，上以其有功，使以檢校司空、同平章事留京師；

translations.literal: Zhongchen fled alone on horseback to the capital; because of his merits the emperor had him remain in the capital as Acting Minister of Works and Co-Grand Councilor;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen fled alone to the capital. Because of his past service, the emperor kept him there as Acting Minister of Works and Co-Grand Councilor;

sentences.zh: 以希烈為蔡州刺史、淮西留後。

translations.literal: Xilie was made Prefect of Cai and acting military governor of Huai-Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was appointed Prefect of Cai and acting military governor of Huai-Xi.

sentences.zh: 以永平節度使李勉兼汴州刺史，增領汴、穎二州，徙鎮汴州。

translations.literal: Yongping military governor Li Mian was concurrently made Prefect of Bian, given charge of the two prefectures Bian and Ying, and transferred his headquarters to Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian, military governor of Yongping, was also made Prefect of Bian, given Bian and Ying prefectures, and moved his headquarters to Bian.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以容管經略使王翃為河中少尹、知府事。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Rongguan pacification commissioner Wang Hong was made Vice Director of Hezhong and charged with governing the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou, Wang Hong, pacification commissioner of Rongguan, was appointed Vice Director of Hezhong and put in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河東副元帥留後部將凌正暴橫，翃抑之。

translations.literal: Hedong deputy commander and acting commander Ling Zheng, a subordinate general, was violent and overbearing; Wang Hong restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Zheng, a subordinate general and acting Hedong deputy commander, was violent and overbearing; Wang Hong kept him in check.

sentences.zh: 正與其徒乘夜作亂，翃知之，故縮漏水數刻以差其期，賊驚，潰走，擒正，誅之，軍府乃安。

translations.literal: Zheng and his followers plotted rebellion by night; Wang Hong learned of it and deliberately shortened the water clock by several quarter-hours to throw off their schedule. The rebels were alarmed, broke and fled; Zheng was captured and executed, and the military government was then secure.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and his followers plotted a night revolt. Wang Hong learned of it and deliberately shortened the water clock by several quarter-hours to throw off their timing. The rebels panicked, broke, and fled; Zheng was captured and executed, and the military government was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使張寶臣既請複姓，又不自安，更請賜姓；

translations.literal: Chengde military governor Zhang Baochen, having already requested to resume his original surname, still did not feel secure and further requested a surname be bestowed;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baochen, military governor of Chengde, had already asked to resume his original surname but still felt uneasy and asked again for an imperial surname;

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，復賜姓李。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guiwei, he was again given the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the day guiwei, he was again granted the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸卯，上始有疾，辛酉，制皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day guimao, the emperor first fell ill; on the day xinyou, he ordered the Crown Prince to oversee state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day guimao, the emperor first fell ill; on the day xinyou he ordered the Crown Prince to oversee state affairs.

sentences.zh: 是夕，上崩於紫宸之內殿，遺詔以郭子儀攝塚宰。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor died in the inner hall of Zichen; his final edict appointed Guo Ziyi as acting chief minister for mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the emperor died in the inner hall of Zichen Palace. His final edict appointed Guo Ziyi acting chief minister for the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，德宗即位，在諒陰中，動遵禮法；

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Dezong took the throne; while in mourning he scrupulously observed ritual and law;
translations.idiomatic: On the day guihai, Dezong took the throne. While in mourning he scrupulously observed ritual and law;

sentences.zh: 嘗召韓王迥食，食馬齒羹，不設鹽、酪。

translations.literal: He once summoned Prince Han Huijing to eat; they ate purslane soup without salt or dairy.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned Prince Han Huijing to dine and served purslane soup without salt or dairy products.

sentences.zh: 常袞性剛急，為政苛細，不合眾心。

translations.literal: Chang Fu was by nature stern and impatient; his governance was harsh and petty and did not accord with popular sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Fu was stern and quick-tempered by nature; his governance was harsh and nitpicking, and he won little favor.

sentences.zh: 時群臣朝夕臨，袞哭委頓，從吏或扶之。

translations.literal: At the time the ministers attended morning and evening; Fu wept in exhaustion and his attendants sometimes supported him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the ministers attended morning and evening; Fu wept until he collapsed, and his attendants sometimes had to support him.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人崔祐甫指以示眾曰：「臣哭君前，有扶禮乎！」

translations.literal: Zhongshu Secretariat Drafter Cui Youfu pointed it out and said to the assembly: "When a minister weeps before his ruler, is there any ritual for being supported!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu, a drafter of the Secretariat, pointed this out and said to the assembly, "When a minister weeps before his ruler, what ritual permits him to be held up!"

sentences.zh: 袞聞，益恨之。

translations.literal: When Fu heard this, he hated Youfu all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu heard this, he hated Youfu all the more.

sentences.zh: 會議群臣喪服，袞以為：「禮，臣為君斬衰三年。

translations.literal: When the ministers convened to discuss mourning garments, Fu held: "By ritual, a minister wears the severest mourning for his ruler for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers met to discuss mourning garments, Fu argued, "By ritual a minister wears the severest mourning for his ruler for three years.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝權制，猶三十六日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han by expedient measure still made it thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, by expedient measure, still fixed it at thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 高宗以來，皆遵漢制。

translations.literal: Since Gaozong, all had followed the Han system.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong onward all had followed the Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗、肅宗之喪，始服二十七日。

translations.literal: Only at the mourning for Xuanzong and Suzong did they begin mourning for twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Only for the mourning of Xuanzong and Suzong did they begin observing twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 今遺詔云：『天下吏人，三日釋服。』

translations.literal: Now the final edict states: 'Officers and commoners throughout the realm, release mourning garments after three days.'
translations.idiomatic: Now the final edict says, 'Officers and commoners throughout the realm shall release mourning garments after three days.'

sentences.zh: 古者卿大夫從君而服，皇帝二十七日而除，在朝群臣亦當如之。」

translations.literal: In antiquity ministers and grandees followed the ruler in mourning; the emperor removed mourning after twenty-seven days, and the ministers at court should likewise."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity ministers and grandees followed the ruler in mourning; the emperor removed mourning after twenty-seven days, and the ministers at court should do the same."

sentences.zh: 祐甫以為：「遺詔，無朝臣、庶人之別。

translations.literal: Youfu held: "The final edict makes no distinction between court ministers and common people.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu argued, "The final edict makes no distinction between court ministers and commoners.

sentences.zh: 朝野中外，莫非天下，凡百執事，孰非吏人！

translations.literal: Court and countryside, within and without—all are the realm; among all who hold office, who is not an officer!
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside, within and without—all are the realm; among all who hold office, who is not an officer!

sentences.zh: 皆應三日釋服。」

translations.literal: All should release mourning garments after three days."
translations.idiomatic: All should release mourning garments after three days."

sentences.zh: 相與力爭，聲色陵厲。

translations.literal: They argued against each other with force; voices and expressions turned fierce.
translations.idiomatic: They argued fiercely, their voices and expressions turning harsh.

sentences.zh: 袞不能堪。

translations.literal: Fu could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 乃奏祐甫率情變禮，請貶潮州刺史；

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized that Youfu had recklessly altered ritual to suit his feelings and requested he be demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou;
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon memorialized that Youfu had willfully altered ritual and asked that he be demoted to Prefect of Chaozhou;

sentences.zh: 上以為太重，閏月，壬申，貶祐甫為河南少尹。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this too severe; in the intercalary month, on the day renshen, Youfu was demoted to Vice Director of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this too harsh; in the intercalary month, on the day renshen, Youfu was demoted to Vice Director of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗之世，天下務殷，宰相常有數人，更直決事，或休沐各歸私第，詔直事者代署其名而奏之，自是踵為故事。

translations.literal: Initially, in the age of Suzong, affairs were pressing throughout the realm; there were often several chief ministers who took turns deciding business, or on days off each returned to his private residence, and an edict had the one on duty sign their names and memorialize—it thereafter became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzong's time affairs pressed hard on the realm; several chief ministers usually took turns deciding business, and on days off each returned home while the one on duty signed their names and submitted memorials—this became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 時郭子儀、朱泚雖以軍功為宰相，皆不預朝政，袞獨居政事堂，代二人署名奏祐甫。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Ziyi and Zhu Ci, though made chief ministers through military merit, both did not participate in court governance; Fu alone occupied the Hall of Administration, signed for the two of them, and memorialized against Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Zhu Ci had been made chief ministers for military merit but took no part in court governance; Fu alone sat in the Hall of Administration, signed for both men, and memorialized against Youfu.

sentences.zh: 祐甫既貶，二人表言其非罪，上問：「卿向言可貶，今雲非罪，何也？」

translations.literal: After Youfu was demoted, the two submitted memorials stating he was not guilty; the emperor asked: "You previously said he should be demoted—now you say he committed no crime. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: After Youfu was demoted, the two submitted memorials saying he was not guilty. The emperor asked, "You previously said he should be demoted—now you say he committed no crime. Why?"

sentences.zh: 二人對，初不知。

translations.literal: The two replied that initially they had not known.
translations.idiomatic: The two replied that at first they had not known.

sentences.zh: 上初即位，以袞為欺罔，大駭。

translations.literal: The emperor had just taken the throne; he regarded Fu's conduct as deception and was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just taken the throne; he saw Fu's conduct as deception and was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，百官衰絰，序立於月華門，有制，貶袞為潮州刺史，以祐甫為門下侍郎、同平章事，聞者震悚。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, the hundred officials in mourning garments stood in order at the Moonlight Gate; an edict demoted Fu to Prefect of Chaozhou and appointed Youfu Grand Secretary of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councilor; those who heard it were shaken with dread.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiaxu the hundred officials in mourning garments stood in order at the Moonlight Gate. An edict demoted Fu to Prefect of Chaozhou and appointed Youfu Grand Secretary of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councilor; all who heard it were shaken.

sentences.zh: 祐甫至昭應而還。

translations.literal: Youfu reached Zhaoying and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu reached Zhaoying and turned back.

sentences.zh: 既而群臣喪服竟用袞議。

translations.literal: Before long the ministers' mourning garments ultimately followed Fu's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the ministers' mourning garments ultimately followed Fu's proposal after all.

sentences.zh: 上時居諒陰，庶政皆委於祐甫，所言無不允。

translations.literal: The emperor was then in mourning; routine government was all entrusted to Youfu, and whatever he said was always approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in mourning and entrusted routine government entirely to Youfu; whatever he proposed was approved.

sentences.zh: 初，至德以後，天下用兵，諸將競論功賞，故官爵不能無濫。

translations.literal: Initially, after the Zhide era, warfare prevailed throughout the realm; generals competed in discussing rewards for merit, so ranks and titles could not be free of excess.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide era warfare engulfed the realm; generals competed for rewards, and ranks and titles could not but be dispensed too freely.

sentences.zh: 及永泰以來，天下稍平，而元載、王縉秉政，四方以賄求官者相屬於門，大者出於載、縉，小者出於卓英倩等，皆如所欲而去。

translations.literal: From the Yongtai era onward the realm grew somewhat peaceful, but Yuan Zai and Wang Jin held power; those from all quarters seeking office through bribes thronged their gates—large cases from Zai and Jin, small ones from Zhuo Yingqian and others—and all departed with what they desired.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongtai era onward the realm grew somewhat peaceful, but Yuan Zai and Wang Jin held power; petitioners from every quarter seeking office through bribes thronged their gates—large bribes to Zai and Jin, smaller ones to Zhuo Yingqian and others—and all left with what they wanted.

sentences.zh: 及常袞為相，思革其弊，杜絕僥倖，四方奏請，一切不與；

translations.literal: When Chang Fu became chief minister, he wished to reform these abuses, cut off opportunism, and rejected all memorials and requests from the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Fu became chief minister he tried to reform these abuses, shut off opportunism, and rejected every petition from the four quarters;

sentences.zh: 而無所甄別，賢愚同滯。

translations.literal: yet without any discrimination, the worthy and the foolish alike were stalled.
translations.idiomatic: but without distinguishing merit from mediocrity, the worthy and the foolish alike were left idle.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫代之，欲收時望，推薦引拔，常無虛日；

translations.literal: Cui Youfu succeeded him, wishing to win popular esteem, recommending and elevating people—hardly a day went by without it;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu succeeded him, eager to win popular esteem, recommending and promoting people almost every day;

sentences.zh: 作相未二百日，除官八百人，前後相矯，終不得其適。

translations.literal: In less than two hundred days as chief minister he appointed eight hundred officials; one after another they competed to outdo each other, and in the end neither approach was right.
translations.idiomatic: In less than two hundred days as chief minister he appointed eight hundred officials; the two ministers had swung from one extreme to the other, and in the end neither course was right.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂佑甫曰：「人或謗卿，所用多涉親故，何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to Youfu: "Some slander you, saying those you employ are largely kinsmen and old associates. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to Youfu, "Some people slander you, saying those you appoint are mostly kinsmen and old associates. Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣為陛下選擇百官，不敢不詳慎，苟平生未之識，何以諳其才行而用之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant selects the hundred officials for Your Majesty and dares not be less than thorough. If I have never known a man in life, how can I know his ability and conduct and employ him?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your servant selects officials for Your Majesty and dares not be careless. If I have never known a man in life, how can I judge his ability and character and appoint him?"

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：臣聞用人者，無親疏、新故之殊，惟賢、不肖之為察。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Your servant has heard that in employing men there should be no distinction of close or distant, new or old—only the discerning of worthy and unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Guang says: I have heard that in employing men one should make no distinction between close and distant, new and old—only between the worthy and the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 其人未必賢也，以親故而取之，固非公也；

translations.literal: When a man is not necessarily worthy, to take him because of kinship or old association is surely not impartial;
translations.idiomatic: When a man is not necessarily worthy, to take him because of kinship or old ties is surely not impartial;

sentences.zh: 苟賢矣，以親故而捨之，亦非公也。

translations.literal: if he is worthy, to set him aside because of kinship or old association is also not impartial.
translations.idiomatic: if he is worthy, to set him aside because of kinship or old ties is also not impartial.

sentences.zh: 夫天下之賢，固非一人所能盡也，若必待素識熟其才行而用之，所遺亦多矣。

translations.literal: The worthy men of the realm surely cannot all be exhausted by one person; if one must wait until one knows them intimately and is familiar with their ability and conduct before employing them, what is lost will also be great.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy men of the realm cannot all be known to one person; if one must wait until one knows a man well and is familiar with his ability and conduct before appointing him, much talent will be lost.

sentences.zh: 古之為相者則不然，舉之以眾，取之以公。

translations.literal: The chief ministers of antiquity were not so—they raised men through the multitude and selected them through impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers of antiquity did otherwise: they relied on the multitude to recommend and on impartiality to choose.

sentences.zh: 眾曰賢矣，己雖不知其詳，姑用之，待其無功，然後退之，有功則進之；

translations.literal: When the multitude said a man was worthy, though they themselves did not know the details, they employed him for the time being; when he achieved nothing they then dismissed him, and when he achieved merit they promoted him;
translations.idiomatic: When the multitude said a man was worthy, though they did not know him in detail they would employ him for the time being; if he achieved nothing they dismissed him, and if he achieved merit they promoted him;

sentences.zh: 所舉得其人則賞之，非其人則罰之。

translations.literal: if their recommendation gained the right man they were rewarded; if not the right man, they were punished.
translations.idiomatic: if a recommendation proved right they were rewarded; if it proved wrong they were punished.

sentences.zh: 進退賞罰，皆眾人所共然也，己不置豪發之私於其間。

translations.literal: Promotion, dismissal, reward, and punishment—all were what the multitude shared in common; they placed not the slightest private interest between.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion, dismissal, reward, and punishment were all matters the multitude shared in common, and they inserted not the slightest private interest.

sentences.zh: 苟推是心以行之，又何遺賢曠官之足病哉！

translations.literal: If one carried this heart forward in practice, how would leaving the worthy unemployed or posts vacant be enough to cause worry!
translations.idiomatic: If one carried this spirit into practice, what worry would there be over neglected talent or vacant posts!

sentences.zh: 詔罷省四方貢獻之不急者，又罷梨園使及樂工三百餘人，所留者悉隸太常。

translations.literal: An edict abolished and reduced unneeded tribute from the four quarters; it also abolished the Pear Garden Commissioner and more than three hundred musicians; those retained were all placed under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished unnecessary tribute from the four quarters and also abolished the Pear Garden Commissioner and more than three hundred musicians; those kept were all placed under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以司徒、中書令領河中尹、靈州大都督、單于、鎮北大都護、關內、河東副元帥、朔方節度、關內支度、鹽池、六城水運大使、押蕃部並營田及河陽道觀察等使，權任既重，功名復大，性寬大，政令頗不肅，代宗欲分其權而難之，久不決。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi as Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Secretariat held concurrently Prefect of Hezhong, Grand Protector of Ling Prefecture, Chanyu, Grand Protector of Zhenbei, deputy commander of Guannei and Hedong, military governor of Shuofang, Guannei supply commissioner, salt ponds, Six Cities water transport commissioner, commissioner for Tibetan tribes and military farms, and Henyang Circuit observation commissioner—his authority and duties were already weighty and his merit and fame again great; he was generous by nature and his government orders were somewhat lax. Daizong wished to divide his power but found it difficult; for long he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, as Minister of Works and Grand Secretary of the Secretariat, also held Prefect of Hezhong, Grand Protector of Ling Prefecture, Chanyu, Grand Protector of Zhenbei, deputy commander of Guannei and Hedong, military governor of Shuofang, Guannei supply commissioner, salt ponds, Six Cities water transport commissioner, commissioner for Tibetan tribes and military farms, and Henyang Circuit observation commissioner. His authority was already immense and his fame towering; he was generous by nature and his orders were somewhat lax. Daizong wished to divide his power but found it difficult and long could not decide.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔尊子儀為尚父，加太尉兼中書令，增實封滿二千戶，月給千五百人糧、二百馬食，子弟、諸婿遷官者十餘人，所領副元帥諸使悉罷之；

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, an edict honored Ziyi as Imperial Father, added Grand Marshal and concurrent Grand Secretary, increased his actual fief to the full two thousand households, granted monthly rations for fifteen hundred men and fodder for two hundred horses, promoted more than ten sons, sons-in-law, and the like, and abolished all the deputy commanderships and commissions he held;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiashen an edict honored Guo Ziyi as Imperial Father, added Grand Marshal and concurrent Grand Secretary, raised his actual fief to the full two thousand households, granted monthly rations for fifteen hundred men and fodder for two hundred horses, promoted more than ten sons and sons-in-law, and abolished all the deputy commanderships and commissions he held;

sentences.zh: 以其裨將河東、朔方都虞候李懷光為河中尹、邠、寧、慶、晉、絳、慈、隰節度使，以朔方留後兼靈州長史常謙光為靈州大都督、西受降城、定遠、天德、鹽、夏、豐等軍州節度使，振武軍使渾瑊為單于大都護、東、中二受降城、振武、鎮北、綏、銀、麟、勝等軍州節度使，分領其任。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Hedong and Shuofang chief commandant Li Huaiguang was made Prefect of Hezhong and military governor of Bin, Ning, Qing, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi; Shuofang acting commander and concurrent Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture Chang Qianguang was made Grand Protector of Ling and military governor of West Shouxiang Fort, Dingyuan, Tiande, Yan, Xia, Feng, and other armies and prefectures; Zhenwu army commissioner Hun Jian was made Grand Protector of Chanyu and military governor of East and Central Shouxiang Forts, Zhenwu, Zhenbei, Sui, Yin, Lin, Sheng, and other armies and prefectures—dividing among them his duties.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate general Li Huaiguang, chief commandant of Hedong and Shuofang, was made Prefect of Hezhong and military governor of Bin, Ning, Qing, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi; Chang Qianguang, acting Shuofang commander and Chief Administrator of Ling Prefecture, was made Grand Protector of Ling and military governor of West Shouxiang Fort, Dingyuan, Tiande, Yan, Xia, Feng, and other armies and prefectures; Hun Jian, commissioner of the Zhenwu army, was made Grand Protector of Chanyu and military governor of the East and Central Shouxiang Forts, Zhenwu, Zhenbei, Sui, Yin, Lin, Sheng, and other armies and prefectures, dividing Guo Ziyi's duties among them.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：「澤州刺史李鷃上《慶雲圖》。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, an edict stated: "Li Yan, Prefect of Ze, submitted a 'Chart of Auspicious Clouds.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu an edict stated, "Li Yan, Prefect of Ze, submitted a 'Chart of Auspicious Clouds.

sentences.zh: 朕以時和年豐為嘉祥，以進賢顯忠為良瑞，如卿雲、靈芝、珍禽、奇獸、怪草、異木，何益於人！

translations.literal: We take timely harmony and abundant harvests as auspicious signs, and promoting the worthy and displaying loyalty as good omens. What benefit do auspicious clouds, spirit fungus, rare birds, exotic beasts, strange plants, and unusual trees bring to the people!
translations.idiomatic: We take timely harmony and abundant harvests as true good omens, and promoting the worthy and displaying loyalty as true auspicious signs. What good do auspicious clouds, spirit fungus, rare birds, exotic beasts, strange plants, and unusual trees do the people!

sentences.zh: 佈告天下，自今有此，無得上獻。」

translations.literal: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm: from now on, when such things appear, none may be submitted to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed throughout the realm: from now on, when such things appear, none may be submitted to the throne."

sentences.zh: 內莊宅使上言諸州有官租萬四千餘斛，上令分給所在充軍儲。

translations.literal: The Director of Inner Manor Properties reported that various prefectures held more than fourteen thousand hu of official rent grain; the emperor ordered it distributed locally for military stores.
