translations.idiomatic: The Director of Inner Manor Properties reported that various prefectures held more than fourteen thousand hu of official rent grain; the emperor ordered it distributed locally for military stores.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸國屢獻馴象，凡四十有二，上曰：「象費豢養而違物性，將安用之！」

translations.literal: Previously, various countries had repeatedly presented tame elephants—forty-two in all. The emperor said: "Elephants cost much to keep and violate their natural disposition—what use shall we make of them!"
translations.idiomatic: Previously various countries had repeatedly presented tame elephants—forty-two in all. The emperor said, "Elephants are costly to keep and violate their nature—what use shall we make of them!"

sentences.zh: 命縱於荊山之陽，及豹、貀、鬥雞、獵犬之類，悉縱之；

translations.literal: He ordered them released on the south side of Mount Jing, and leopards, badgers, fighting cocks, hunting dogs, and the like were all released as well;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them released on the south side of Mount Jing, and leopards, badgers, fighting cocks, hunting dogs, and the like were all released as well;

sentences.zh: 又出宮女數百人。

translations.literal: He also released several hundred palace women.
translations.idiomatic: He also released several hundred palace women.

sentences.zh: 於是中外皆悅，淄青軍士，至投兵相顧曰「明主出矣，吾屬猶反乎！」

translations.literal: Thereupon all within and without were pleased; soldiers of Ziqing even cast aside their weapons, looked at one another, and said, "An enlightened ruler has appeared—shall we still rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all within and without rejoiced; soldiers of Ziqing even cast aside their weapons, looked at one another, and said, "An enlightened ruler has appeared—shall we still rebel!"

sentences.zh: 戊子，以淮西留後李希烈為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Huai-Xi acting commander Li Xilie was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, Li Xilie, acting commander of Huai-Xi, was made military governor.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以河陽鎮遏使馬燧為河東節度使。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Heyang suppression commissioner Ma Sui was made Hedong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, Ma Sui, suppression commissioner of Heyang, was made military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東承百井之敗，騎士單弱，燧悉召牧馬廝役，得數千人，教之數月，皆為精騎。

translations.literal: Hedong, bearing the defeat at Baijing, had cavalry that was few and weak; Sui summoned all horse-herders and stable hands, got several thousand men, trained them for several months, and all became elite cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong, still smarting from the defeat at Baijing, had cavalry that was few and weak; Sui summoned all horse-herders and stable hands, gathered several thousand men, trained them for several months, and turned them all into elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 造甲必為長短三等，稱其所衣，以便進趨。

translations.literal: When making armor he always made three grades of length, matched to what the wearers wore, to facilitate advance and charge.
translations.idiomatic: When making armor he always made three lengths to match the wearers' height, so they could advance and charge with ease.

sentences.zh: 又造戰車，行則載兵甲，止則為營陳，或塞險以遏奔沖；

translations.literal: He also made war chariots: when marching they carried arms and armor; when halting they formed encampments; or they blocked narrow passes to check sudden charges;
translations.idiomatic: He also built war chariots that carried arms and armor on the march, formed encampments when halted, and could block narrow passes to check sudden charges;

sentences.zh: 器械無不精利。

translations.literal: No weapon or tool failed to be finely honed.
translations.idiomatic: Every weapon and tool was made with precision.

sentences.zh: 居一年，得選兵三萬。

translations.literal: After one year he had thirty thousand selected troops.
translations.idiomatic: After one year he had thirty thousand picked troops.

sentences.zh: 辟兗州人張建封為判官，署李自良代州刺史，委任之。

translations.literal: He recruited Zhang Jianfeng of Yan Prefecture as administrative aide, appointed Li Ziliang Prefect of Dai, and entrusted them with responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Zhang Jianfeng of Yan Prefecture as administrative aide, appointed Li Ziliang Prefect of Dai, and entrusted them with real authority.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎黎幹，狡險諛佞，與宦官特進劉忠翼相親善。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Li Gan was crafty, treacherous, and sycophantic, and was close to the eunuch Special Advance Liu Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, Vice Minister of War, was crafty, treacherous, and sycophantic, and was on close terms with the eunuch Special Advance Liu Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 忠翼本名清潭，恃寵貪縱。

translations.literal: Zhongyi's original name was Qingtan; relying on favor he was greedy and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi's original name was Qingtan; relying on imperial favor he was greedy and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 二人皆為眾所惡。

translations.literal: Both men were detested by all.
translations.idiomatic: Both were detested by all.

sentences.zh: 時人或言幹、忠翼嘗勸代宗立獨孤貴妃為皇后，妃子韓王迥為太子。

translations.literal: At the time some said Gan and Zhongyi had once urged Daizong to establish Consort Dugu as empress and her son Prince Han Huijing as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some said Gan and Zhongyi had once urged Daizong to make Consort Dugu empress and her son Prince Han Huijing crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上即位，幹密乘輿詣忠翼謀事；

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, Gan secretly rode the imperial carriage to Zhongyi's to plot affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Gan secretly took the imperial carriage to Zhongyi's residence to plot;

sentences.zh: 事覺，丙申、幹、忠翼並除名長流，至藍田，賜死。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light, on the day bingshen Gan and Zhongyi were both stripped of rank and exiled far; reaching Lantian, they were granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot came to light, on the day bingshen Gan and Zhongyi were both stripped of rank and exiled far; at Lantian they were granted death.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎判度支韓滉為太常卿，以吏部尚書劉晏判度支。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue and acting Commissioner of Finance Han Huang was made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; Minister of Personnel Liu Yan was made acting Commissioner of Finance.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting Commissioner of Finance, was made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; Liu Yan, Minister of Personnel, was made acting Commissioner of Finance.

sentences.zh: 先是晏、滉分掌天下財賦，晏掌河南、山南、江淮、嶺南，滉掌關內，河東、劍南，至是，晏始兼之。

translations.literal: Previously Yan and Huang had divided control of the realm's revenues—Yan controlled Henan, Shannan, Jiang-Huai, and Lingnan; Huang controlled Guannei, Hedong, and Jiannan. Now Yan for the first time held both.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Yan and Huang had divided control of the realm's revenues: Yan controlled Henan, Shannan, Jiang-Huai, and Lingnan, while Huang controlled Guannei, Hedong, and Jiannan. Now Yan held both for the first time.

sentences.zh: 上素聞滉掊克過甚，故罷其利權，尋出為晉州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard that Huang's exactions were excessive, so he removed his financial authority and soon sent him out as Prefect of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long heard that Huang's exactions were excessive, so he removed his financial authority and soon sent him out as Prefect of Jin.

sentences.zh: 至德初，第五琦始榷鹽以佐軍用，及劉晏代之，法益精密，初歲入錢六十萬緡，末年所入逾十倍，而人不厭苦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, Diwu Qi first monopolized salt to aid military expenditure; when Liu Yan succeeded him the law grew more precise, revenue in the first year was six hundred thousand strings of cash, and in the final year income exceeded that tenfold—yet the people did not resent it bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhide, Diwu Qi first monopolized salt to support military expenditure; when Liu Yan succeeded him the system grew more precise. Revenue in the first year was six hundred thousand strings of cash, and in the final year it exceeded that tenfold—yet the people did not resent it bitterly.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，計一歲徵賦所入總一千二百萬緡，而鹽利居其太半。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, calculated annual tax and levy receipts totaled twelve million strings of cash, and salt profits made up more than half.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dali, annual tax and levy receipts totaled twelve million strings of cash, and salt profits made up more than half.

sentences.zh: 以鹽為漕傭，自江、淮至渭橋，率萬斛傭七千緡，自淮以北，列置巡院，擇能吏主之，不煩州縣而集事。

translations.literal: Using salt revenue for transport hire, from Jiang-Huai to Weiqiao the rate was seven thousand strings per ten thousand hu; north of the Huai, inspection posts were set up in series, capable officials chosen to manage them, and affairs were handled without troubling prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Salt revenue paid for transport hire: from Jiang-Huai to Weiqiao the rate was seven thousand strings per ten thousand hu. North of the Huai, inspection posts were set up in series under capable officials, and affairs were handled without troubling prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 六月，己亥朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the new moon of jihai, an amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the new moon of jihai, an amnesty was granted throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 西川節度使崔寧、永平節度使李勉並同平章事。

translations.literal: Xichuan military governor Cui Ning and Yongping military governor Li Mian were both made Co-Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ning, military governor of Xichuan, and Li Mian, military governor of Yongping, were both made Co-Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 詔：「天下冤滯，州府不為理，聽詣三司使，以中丞、舍人、給事中各一人，日於朝堂受詞。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Where wrongs and delays exist throughout the realm and prefectures will not adjudicate them, petitioners may go to the Three Offices Commissioner, with one censor, one drafter, and one palace adviser each day receiving petitions in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Where wrongs and delays exist throughout the realm and prefectures will not adjudicate them, petitioners may go to the Three Offices Commissioner, with one censor, one drafter, and one palace adviser each day receiving petitions in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 推決尚未盡者，聽撾登聞鼓。

translations.literal: Those whose cases have not yet been fully decided may strike the Petition drum.
translations.idiomatic: Those whose cases have not yet been fully decided may strike the Petition drum.

sentences.zh: 自今無得復奏置寺觀及請度僧尼。」

translations.literal: From now on no one may again memorialize to establish temples or monasteries or request ordination of monks and nuns."
translations.idiomatic: From now on no one may again memorialize to establish temples or monasteries or request ordination of monks and nuns."

sentences.zh: 於是撾登聞鼓者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon very many people struck the Petition drum.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon very many people struck the Petition drum.

sentences.zh: 右金吾將軍裴諝上疏，以為：「訟者所爭皆細故，若天子一一親之，則安用吏理乎！」

translations.literal: Right Jinwu General Pei Xu submitted a memorial, holding: "What litigants dispute are all petty matters—if the Son of Heaven personally handles each one, what need is there for officials to govern!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xu, Right Jinwu General, submitted a memorial arguing, "What litigants dispute are all petty matters—if the Son of Heaven personally handles each one, what need is there for officials to govern!"

sentences.zh: 上乃悉歸之有司。

translations.literal: The emperor then returned them all to the appropriate offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then returned them all to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 制：「應山陵制度，務從優厚，當竭帑藏以供其費。」

translations.literal: An edict stated: "For the regulations governing the imperial tomb, everything should be as generous as possible; the treasury should be exhausted to supply the expense."
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "For the regulations governing the imperial tomb, everything should be as generous as possible; the treasury should be exhausted to supply the expense."

sentences.zh: 刑部員外郎令孤峘上疏諫，其略曰：「臣伏讀遺詔，務從儉約，若制度優厚，豈顧命之意邪！」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Linghu Dan submitted a memorial of remonstrance; in summary he said: "Your servant has reverently read the final testament, which urged frugality; if the regulations are generous, how can that accord with the dying command!"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Linghu Dan submitted a memorial of remonstrance; in summary he said: "Your servant has reverently read the final testament, which urged frugality. If the regulations are generous, how can that accord with the dying command!"

sentences.zh: 上答詔，略曰：「非唯中朕之病，抑亦成朕之美，敢不聞義而徙！」

translations.literal: The emperor replied by edict; in summary he said: "This not only hits my fault but also completes my virtue—how dare I not move upon hearing what is right!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied by edict; in summary he said: "This not only hits my fault but also completes my virtue—how dare I not move upon hearing what is right!"

sentences.zh: 峘，德棻之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Dan was the great-great-grandson of Defen.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was the great-great-grandson of Defen.

sentences.zh: 庚子，立皇子誦為宣王，謨為舒王，諶為通王，諒為虔王，詳為肅王。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the imperial sons were enfeoffed: Song as Prince of Xuan, Mo as Prince of Shu, Chen as Prince of Tong, Liang as Prince of Qian, and Xiang as Prince of Su.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, the imperial sons were enfeoffed: Song as Prince of Xuan, Mo as Prince of Shu, Chen as Prince of Tong, Liang as Prince of Qian, and Xiang as Prince of Su.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，立皇弟乃為益王，傀為蜀王。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Nai as Prince of Yi and Gui as Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, the emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Nai as Prince of Yi and Gui as Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 丙午，舉先天事故，六品以上清望官，雖非供奉、侍衛之官，日令二人更直待制，以備顧問。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, following the precedent of the Xiantian era, for officials of sixth rank and above of clear reputation, even if not in attendance or guard posts, two men each day were ordered to rotate on duty awaiting imperial command, to be ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu, following the precedent of the Xiantian era, officials of sixth rank and above with clear reputations—even if not in attendance or guard posts—were ordered to have two men rotate on duty each day awaiting imperial command, to be ready for consultation.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以朱泚為鳳翔尹。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Zhu Ci was made Prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, Zhu Ci was appointed Prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 代宗優寵宦官，奉使四方者，不禁其求取。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong favored and indulged eunuchs; those sent on missions to the four directions were not forbidden to solicit gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong favored and indulged eunuchs, and those sent on missions to the four directions were not forbidden to solicit gifts.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣中使賜妃族，還，問所得頗少，代宗不悅，以為輕我命。

translations.literal: He once sent a palace envoy to bestow gifts on a consort's clan; when the envoy returned, he asked what had been received and found it rather little; Daizong was displeased, thinking his command had been slighted.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent a palace envoy to bestow gifts on a consort's clan. When the envoy returned, he asked what had been received and found it rather little. Daizong was displeased, thinking his command had been slighted.

sentences.zh: 妃懼，遽以私物償之。

translations.literal: The consort was afraid and hastily compensated with her private goods.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was afraid and hastily compensated with her private goods.

sentences.zh: 由是中使公求賂遺，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: From this, palace envoys openly solicited bribes and gifts without any fear.
translations.idiomatic: From this, palace envoys openly solicited bribes and gifts without fear.

sentences.zh: 宰相嘗貯錢於閣中，每賜一物，宣一旨，無徒還者；

translations.literal: Chancellors would store money in their offices; for every gift bestowed or every edict announced, none returned empty-handed;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors would store money in their offices; for every gift bestowed or every edict announced, none returned empty-handed;

sentences.zh: 出使所歷州縣，移文取貨，與賦稅同，皆重載而歸。

translations.literal: On missions they passed through prefectures and counties, sent official documents to collect goods equal to taxes, and all returned heavily laden.
translations.idiomatic: On missions they passed through prefectures and counties, sent official documents to collect goods equal to taxes, and all returned heavily laden.

sentences.zh: 上素知其弊。

translations.literal: The emperor had long known this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long known of this abuse.

sentences.zh: 遣中使邵光超賜李希烈旌節；

translations.literal: He sent palace envoy Shao Guangchao to bestow the banner and credentials on Li Xilie;
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace envoy Shao Guangchao to bestow the banner and credentials on Li Xilie;

sentences.zh: 希烈贈之僕、馬及縑七百匹，黃茗二百斤。

translations.literal: Xilie gave him servants, horses, seven hundred bolts of silk, and two hundred jin of yellow tea.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie gave him servants, horses, seven hundred bolts of silk, and two hundred jin of yellow tea.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，怒，杖光超六十而流之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was enraged, had Guangchao beaten sixty strokes and banished.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he was enraged, had Guangchao beaten sixty strokes, and banished him.

sentences.zh: 於是中使之未歸者，皆潛棄所得於山谷，雖與之，莫敢受。

translations.literal: Thereupon palace envoys who had not yet returned all secretly discarded their gains in valleys and mountains; even when gifts were offered, none dared accept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon palace envoys who had not yet returned all secretly discarded their gains in valleys and mountains. Even when gifts were offered, none dared accept.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以神策都知兵馬使、右領軍大將軍王駕鶴為東都園苑使，以司農卿白琇珪代之，更名志貞。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Wang Jiahe, Chief Military Commissioner of the Shence Army and General of the Right Imperial Guard, was made Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Gardens; Minister of Agriculture Bai Xiugui replaced him and was renamed Zhizhen.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi, Wang Jiahe, Chief Military Commissioner of the Shence Army and General of the Right Imperial Guard, was made Commissioner of the Eastern Capital Gardens. Minister of Agriculture Bai Xiugui replaced him and was renamed Zhizhen.

sentences.zh: 駕鶴典禁兵十餘年，權行中外，詔下，上恐其生變；

translations.literal: Jiahe had commanded the palace army for more than ten years and wielded authority at court and abroad; when the edict was issued, the emperor feared he might cause trouble;
translations.idiomatic: Jiahe had commanded the palace army for more than ten years and wielded authority at court and abroad. When the edict was issued, the emperor feared he might cause trouble;

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫召駕鶴與語，留連久之，琇珪已視事矣。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu summoned Jiahe to converse and detained him for a long while; Xiugui had already assumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu summoned Jiahe to converse and detained him for a long while, by which time Xiugui had already assumed office.

sentences.zh: 李正己畏上威名，表獻錢三十萬緡；

translations.literal: Li Zhengji feared the emperor's prestige and submitted a memorial offering three hundred thousand strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji feared the emperor's prestige and submitted a memorial offering three hundred thousand strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 上欲受之，恐見欺，卻之則無辭。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to accept it but feared being deceived; to refuse it would leave him without grounds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to accept it but feared being deceived; to refuse it would leave him without grounds.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫請遣使慰勞淄青將士，因以正己所獻錢賜之，使將士人人戴上恩；

translations.literal: Cui Youfu requested sending envoys to comfort the Ziqing officers and soldiers, and thereby bestow on them the money Zhengji had offered, so that every officer and soldier would bear the emperor's grace;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu requested sending envoys to comfort the Ziqing officers and soldiers and bestow on them the money Zhengji had offered, so that every officer and soldier would bear the emperor's grace;

sentences.zh: 又諸道聞之，知朝廷不重貨財。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the various circuits heard of it, they would know the court did not value wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the various circuits heard of it, they would know the court did not value wealth.

sentences.zh: 上悅，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and followed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and followed the plan.

sentences.zh: 正己大慚服。

translations.literal: Zhengji was greatly ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji was greatly ashamed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 天下以為太平之治，庶幾可望焉。

translations.literal: All under heaven thought that governance of peace might soon be within reach.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven thought that governance of peace might soon be within reach.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the new moon of the day wuchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the new moon of wuchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 禮儀使、吏部尚書顏真卿上言：「上元中，政在宮壺，始增祖宗之謚。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenqing, Commissioner of Ritual and Minister of Personnel, submitted a memorial: "In the Shangyuan era, when government lay in the empress's hands, posthumous titles of the ancestors were first augmented.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing, Commissioner of Ritual and Minister of Personnel, submitted a memorial: "In the Shangyuan era, when government lay in the empress's hands, posthumous titles of the ancestors were first augmented.

sentences.zh: 玄宗末，奸臣竊命，累聖之謚，有加至十一字者。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, treacherous ministers usurped authority; posthumous titles of successive emperors were increased to as many as eleven characters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, treacherous ministers usurped authority, and posthumous titles of successive emperors were increased to as many as eleven characters.

sentences.zh: 按周之文、武，言文不稱武，言武不稱文，豈盛德所不優乎？

translations.literal: Consider the Zhou kings Wen and Wu: when speaking of Wen one does not call him Wu, when speaking of Wu one does not call him Wen—is this not because their supreme virtue cannot be surpassed?
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Zhou kings Wen and Wu: when speaking of Wen one does not call him Wu, when speaking of Wu one does not call him Wen—is this not because their supreme virtue cannot be surpassed?

sentences.zh: 蓋群臣稱其至者故也。

translations.literal: It is because the assembled ministers called them to the utmost, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: It is because the assembled ministers called them to the utmost, that is all.

sentences.zh: 故謚多不為褒，少不為貶。

translations.literal: Therefore many characters in a posthumous title do not mean more praise, and few do not mean less praise.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore many characters in a posthumous title do not mean more praise, and few do not mean less praise.

sentences.zh: 今累聖謚號太廣，有逾古制，請自中宗以上皆從初謚，睿宗曰聖真皇帝，玄宗曰孝明皇帝，肅宗曰宣皇帝，以省文尚質，正名敦本。」

translations.literal: Now the posthumous titles of successive emperors are too broad and exceed ancient regulations. I request that from Emperor Zhongzong upward all revert to the initial posthumous titles: Ruizong as Emperor Sheng Zhen, Xuanzong as Emperor Xiao Ming, and Suzong as Emperor Xuan—to simplify the text, honor substance, correct names, and strengthen fundamentals."
translations.idiomatic: Now the posthumous titles of successive emperors are too broad and exceed ancient regulations. I request that from Emperor Zhongzong upward all revert to the initial posthumous titles: Ruizong as Emperor Sheng Zhen, Xuanzong as Emperor Xiao Ming, and Suzong as Emperor Xuan—to simplify the text, honor substance, correct names, and strengthen fundamentals."

sentences.zh: 上命百官集議，儒學之士，皆從真卿議；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation; scholars of Confucian learning all followed Zhenqing's proposal;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all officials to assemble for deliberation; scholars of Confucian learning all followed Zhenqing's proposal;

sentences.zh: 獨兵部侍郎袁參，官以兵進，奏言：「陵廟玉冊、木主皆已刊勒，不可輕改，」事遂寢。

translations.literal: Only Vice Minister of War Yuan Can, whose office had risen through military service, memorialized: "The jade tablets and wooden spirit tablets in the imperial tombs and temples have already been carved and engraved and cannot lightly be changed." The matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Vice Minister of War Yuan Can, whose office had risen through military service, memorialized: "The jade tablets and wooden spirit tablets in the imperial tombs and temples have already been carved and engraved and cannot lightly be changed." The matter thereupon lapsed.

sentences.zh: 不知陵中玉冊所刻，乃初謚也。

translations.literal: He did not know that what was carved on the jade tablets in the tombs was the initial posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He did not know that what was carved on the jade tablets in the tombs was the initial posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 初，代宗之世，事多留滯，四夷使者及四方奏計，或連歲不遣，乃於右銀台門置客省以處之；

translations.literal: Initially, in Emperor Daizong's reign, affairs were often delayed; envoys of the four barbarians and memorialists reporting accounts from the four directions were sometimes not dismissed for years on end; therefore a Guest Reception Office was set up at the Right Yintai Gate to house them;
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Emperor Daizong's reign, affairs were often delayed. Envoys of the four barbarians and memorialists reporting accounts from the four directions were sometimes not dismissed for years on end, so a Guest Reception Office was set up at the Right Yintai Gate to house them;

sentences.zh: 及上書言事孟浪者、失職未敘者，亦置其中，動經十歲。

translations.literal: Those who submitted memorials on affairs rashly and those who had lost office and not yet been reappointed were also placed there, often for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submitted memorials on affairs rashly and those who had lost office and not yet been reappointed were also placed there, often for ten years.

sentences.zh: 常有數百人，並部曲、畜產動以千計，度支廩給，其費甚廣。

translations.literal: There were often several hundred men, together with retainers and livestock numbering in the thousands; the Finance Commission supplied grain rations, and the expense was very great.
translations.idiomatic: There were often several hundred men, together with retainers and livestock numbering in the thousands. The Finance Commission supplied grain rations, and the expense was very great.

sentences.zh: 上悉命疏理，拘者出之，事竟者遣之，當敘者任之，歲省谷萬九千二百斛。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a full review: the detained were released, those whose business was finished were sent away, those due for reappointment were given office; grain saved that year amounted to nineteen thousand two hundred hu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a full review: the detained were released, those whose business was finished were sent away, and those due for reappointment were given office. Grain saved that year amounted to nineteen thousand two hundred hu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，毀元載、馬璘、劉忠翼之第。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, the mansions of Yuan Zai, Ma Lin, and Liu Zhongyi were demolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen, the mansions of Yuan Zai, Ma Lin, and Liu Zhongyi were demolished.

sentences.zh: 初，天寶中，貴戚第捨雖極奢麗，而坦屋高下，猶存制度，然李靖家廟已為楊氏馬廄矣。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Tianbao era, though the mansions of the imperial kin were extremely luxurious, the heights of flat-roofed halls still preserved regulations; yet Li Jing's ancestral temple had already become the Yang clan's stable.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the Tianbao era, though the mansions of the imperial kin were extremely luxurious, the heights of flat-roofed halls still preserved regulations; yet Li Jing's ancestral temple had already become the Yang clan's stable.

sentences.zh: 及安、史亂後，法度墮弛，大臣、將帥、宦官競治第捨，各窮其力而後止，時人謂之木妖。

translations.literal: After the An-Shi rebellion, laws and regulations collapsed; great ministers, generals, and eunuchs competed in building mansions, each exhausting his strength before stopping; people of the time called them wooden demons.
translations.idiomatic: After the An-Shi rebellion, laws and regulations collapsed. Great ministers, generals, and eunuchs competed in building mansions, each exhausting his strength before stopping; people of the time called them wooden demons.

sentences.zh: 上素疾之，故毀其尤者，仍命馬氏獻其園，隸宮司，謂之奉成園。

translations.literal: The emperor had long detested this; therefore he demolished the worst offenders and ordered the Ma clan to present its garden, placing it under palace administration and calling it the Garden of Reverent Completion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long detested this; therefore he demolished the worst offenders and ordered the Ma clan to present its garden, placing it under palace administration and calling it the Garden of Reverent Completion.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，減常貢宮中服用錦千匹、服玩數千事。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, the regular tribute of a thousand bolts of palace silk and several thousand items of clothing and ornaments was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, the regular tribute of a thousand bolts of palace silk and several thousand items of clothing and ornaments was reduced.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔回紇諸胡在京師者，各服其服，無得效華人。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, an edict ordered the various Hu of the Uighurs in the capital each to wear their own dress and not imitate Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, an edict ordered the various Hu of the Uighurs in the capital each to wear their own dress and not imitate Chinese.

sentences.zh: 先是回紇留京師者常千人，商胡偽服而雜居者又倍之，縣官日給饔餼，殖資產，開第捨，市肆美利皆歸之，日縱暴橫，吏不敢問。

translations.literal: Earlier, Uighurs remaining in the capital were often a thousand men; merchant Hu who wore Chinese dress in disguise and lived among them were twice as many. The county officials daily supplied meals; they accumulated assets, opened mansions, and all the best profits of the markets fell to them; daily they committed violence and arrogance, and officials dared not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Uighurs remaining in the capital were often a thousand men, and merchant Hu who wore Chinese dress in disguise and lived among them were twice as many. County officials daily supplied their meals. They accumulated assets, opened mansions, and all the best profits of the markets fell to them. Daily they committed violence and arrogance, and officials dared not inquire.

sentences.zh: 或衣華服，誘取妻妾，故禁之。

translations.literal: Some wore Chinese dress and enticed women to become wives and concubines; therefore this was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Some wore Chinese dress and enticed women to become wives and concubines; therefore this was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，罷天下榷酒收利。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the monopoly on wine and collection of profits throughout the realm was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao, the monopoly on wine and collection of profits throughout the realm was abolished.

sentences.zh: 上之在東宮也，國子博士河中張涉為侍讀，即位之夕，召涉入禁中，事無大小皆咨之；

translations.literal: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Zhang She of Hezhong, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, served as tutor; on the night of his accession he summoned She into the inner palace and consulted him on affairs great and small;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Zhang She of Hezhong, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, served as tutor. On the night of his accession he summoned She into the inner palace and consulted him on affairs great and small;

sentences.zh: 明日，置於翰林為學士，親重無比。

translations.literal: The next day he placed him in the Hanlin Academy as academician; his intimacy and favor were unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he placed him in the Hanlin Academy as academician; his intimacy and favor were unmatched.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以涉為右散騎常侍，仍為學士。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, She was made Right Regular Attendant and continued as academician.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiwei, She was appointed Right Regular Attendant and continued as academician.
